web_blocks.title: 8.1 Confirmed Weinstein Stage 4 Breakdown Across Every Timeframe

web_blocks.html: The technical tape confirms every fundamental caution. As of the November 24, 2026 close, AMD sits in an unambiguous Weinstein Stage 4 downtrend (entry_timing_posture: AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN; technical_timing_gate: CAP_REJECTED) [28]. Closing at $387.65 (down 6.20% on the session, -23.97% over 1 week, and -25.85% over 1 month), AMD has sliced cleanly below every institutional moving average: -29.26% below its 50-day SMA ($547.98), -23.38% below its 30-week SMA ($505.92), -19.97% below its 10-week EMA ($484.39), and -10.45% below its 200-day SMA ($432.87) [28].

Multi-timeframe momentum confirms active liquidation rather than a constructive pullback. Daily RSI(14) sits at 36.41 (options feed 36.34), 4-hour RSI(14) is depressed at 33.12 with no intraday reversal (intraday_4h_turn: false), and weekly RSI(14) has rolled down to 41.81 [28]. Average True Range (ATR-14) has expanded to $46.51 (12.0% of price!), reflecting violent institutional repricing after the November 23 Form S-3ASR 336.9-million-share resale registration [26][28]. The broader market offers zero tailwind. The S&P 500 is in a Downtrend with 10 distribution days and 27.8% breadth above the 50-DMA. Semiconductor breadth has collapsed to just 2.1% above the 50-DMA and 6.2% above the 200-DMA [28].

web_blocks.title: 8.2 Multi-Timeframe Technical Ledger & Key Structural Levels

web_blocks.html: AMD is now sitting directly on top of its classic Pivot S2 major structural shelf at $385.53 [28]. Below $385.53, air pockets open rapidly toward the $335–$355 prior breakout congestion zone and the 52-week low at $188.22. Overhead supply is massive: any reflex bounce faces layered institutional selling at the 200-day SMA ($432.87), Pivot S1 ($445.17), the 10-week EMA ($484.39), and the 30-week SMA ($505.92) [28]. Until AMD stops making lower lows, carves a multi-week Stage 1 base, and reclaims its 30-week SMA on expanding volume, rallies are counter-trend traps.

web_blocks.title: 8.3 Institutional Flow, Short Interest & Options Structure

web_blocks.html: Institutional ownership remains high at 75.37% (down 1.03% over the recent quarter), while insider ownership is minimal at 0.51% with -5.29% net insider selling [27]. Short interest sits at a modest 3.00% of float (49.01 million shares, 1.75 days to cover) [27], confirming that this 41% drawdown is driven by long-only institutional de-risking and S-3ASR supply fears rather than a crowded short squeeze setup. In the options market, 20-day realized volatility (135.4% HV20) dwarfs at-the-money implied volatility (84.7% IV), creating an IV_CHEAP regime. However, as detailed in our deterministic Options Overlay below, buying naked calls into an active Stage 4 knife-drop is a theta trap; the options engine stamps WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT_OR_BASE, conditionally modeling a defined-risk Feb 19, 2027 $390/$610 Bull Call Spread ($52.59 debit) only if AMD stabilizes above $385.53.

book_paragraphs: Now let us open the chart together. If Chapter 7 gave you pause on valuation, Chapter 8 slams the brakes completely. AMD is not in a gentle pullback inside an uptrend. It is in a textbook Weinstein Stage 4 breakdown.

Look at the numbers from the November 24 close. At $387.65, AMD sits nearly 24% below its 30-week moving average, 29% below its 50-day moving average, and more than 10% below its 200-day moving average. It has lost 24% of its value in a single week and 41% from its $658.52 high. Every time a stock slices through its 200-day average on expanding ten-day volume—48 million shares a day versus a 37-million thirty-day norm—institutions are not quietly accumulating. They are heading for the exits.

And notice the neighborhood. This is not an isolated stumble in a roaring bull market. The S&P 500 is sitting in a ten-distribution-day Downtrend with just 27.8% of stocks above their 50-day average. Inside the Semiconductor sector itself, only 2.1% of stocks are above their 50-day moving average. Trying to catch a falling knife when 98% of the sector is underwater is a low-probability gamble.

Right now, AMD is perched precariously on its $385.53 Pivot S2 shelf. Could it bounce $30 or $40 on an oversold reflex? Of course—its 14-day Average True Range is $46.51! That is a 12% daily swing range. Volatility that wide destroys undisciplined stop-losses and whipsaws short-term traders. Even our deterministic options engine says to stand aside: wait for the storm to pass, let a real Stage 1 base form, and never fight a broken weekly trend.

Let us zoom in on the multi-timeframe anatomy of this breakdown—weekly, daily, and four-hour—because Stan Weinstein's stage framework exists specifically to save us from buying great stories at the worst possible moment. On the weekly chart, AMD spent much of 2026 surging toward its $658.52 peak as investors celebrated the OpenAI and Meta 6-gigawatt agreements. That Stage 2 advance peaked and rolled into a violent Stage 3 top before slicing cleanly through the 30-week simple moving average at $505.92 and the 10-week exponential moving average at $484.39. Weekly RSI has dropped to 41.81, confirming that institutional momentum has flipped from accumulation to distribution.

Drop down to the daily chart and the damage looks even starker. On November 24, 2026, AMD fell 6.20% to close at $387.65. That puts the stock 29.26% below its 50-day SMA ($547.98), 20.61% below its 20-day SMA ($488.30), and 10.45% below its 200-day SMA ($432.87). Notice the volume footprint: over the past ten sessions, average daily volume jumped to 48.09 million shares—nearly 29% above the 30-day average of 37.38 million shares. Heavy volume during a 24% one-week drop is classic institutional liquidation triggered by the November 23 Form S-3ASR resale shelf and broader AI chip de-risking.

Now check the four-hour intraday tape. Some active traders try to front-run Stage 4 bottoms by hunting for a four-hour bullish divergence or a reclaim of the 4-hour 20-EMA. Look at our live TradingView snapshot: AMD's 4-hour RSI sits at 33.12, the 4-hour 20-EMA sits way overhead at $466.70, and the 4-hour 50-SMA sits at $501.22. There is zero intraday reversal signal (intraday_4h_turn is false). Every bounce attempt over the past two weeks has been sold into.

Look closely at the ownership and short-interest structure too, because it tells us who is selling. Institutional ownership sits at 75.37%, while insiders own just 0.51% and sold net shares (-5.29%). Short interest is a quiet 3.00% of float—just 49 million shares or 1.75 days to cover. That matters enormously. When a stock drops 41% with 25% short interest, you can get a violent short-covering rally. When a stock drops 41% with only 3% short interest, it means long-only mutual funds and hedge funds are actively lightening up—and there is no crowded short base forced to buy them out.

Finally, let us check the options chain in plain dollars. Even though 20-day realized volatility (135.4% HV20) exceeds implied volatility (84.7% IV), our risk audit stamps NO_OPTIONS_EDGE. A single February 19, 2027 $390/$610 Bull Call Spread costs $5,259 upfront—6.30% of your $83,506.98 net worth and 72.1% of your cash—while needing $442.59 just to break even in 86 days, well above our $375 Base fair value. At $387.65 with a $46.51 ATR and 98% of semiconductor stocks below their 50-day average, standing completely aside is the only disciplined move.

book_callouts.text: When a stock drops 24% in five sessions with a $46.51 ATR, patience is a weapon. You do not get extra points for buying the exact tick of the bottom—you protect your capital by waiting for institutions to prove they are done selling.
